predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: 'Asia Minor' (north of the Taurus) that Antiochus Hierax demanded from his brother Seleucus II

successors.name: Kingdom of Pergamon
successors.text: 'putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains', which Attalus I gained after his victories of c.

ledger.x: 240: Antiochus Hierax sets himself up as king in Asia Minor against Seleucus II.
240: Seleucus II turns on his brother once peace with Ptolemy is made.
237: Seleucus II gives up Asia Minor.
230: Attalus I of Pergamon takes on Hierax and his Galatian allies.

228: Attalus's run of victories over Hierax includes the battle 'near Sardis in the spring of 228 BC' (Attalus I page); the last fight it names, the Battle of the Harpasus in Caria, is undated, so the war is closed in 228.
228: Hierax loses Asia Minor to Pergamon.
228: Hierax is left without land; he is 'killed in Thrace in 226 BC' (the Seleucus II page: 'killed by robbers in c.

wars.name: War of the Brothers (Seleucid civil war)
Attalus I's war against Antiochus Hierax and the Galatians
wars.outcome: Attalus won at Aphrodisium and three more battles, one 'near Sardis in the spring of 228 BC', and gained 'putative control over all of Seleucid Asia Minor north of the Taurus Mountains'.

certainty.note: Hierax's land is a reading of 'Asia Minor north of the Taurus'; no page gives a frontier.
